transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… well, I guess I’m here because my husband thinks I should talk to someone, and people at work are acting like I’m making things up. I don’t want to sound difficult or anything, but at the warehouse it feels pretty clear they’ve been watching what I do and changing the pallet counts so I don’t get the supervisor spot. My husband keeps saying I’m just stressed, but… I know what I’m seeing. Is that okay to say?
Do you think someone is actually following or watching you outside of work?

I mean… outside of work, I don’t know if I’d say “following,” exactly. I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is. But at the warehouse, yes, it feels like they’re watching what I do, keeping track of my moves, and then the pallet counts come out different so I don’t get that supervisor spot. That’s why I came in, really—my husband and them keep acting like I’m crazy, but I know what I’ve been seeing. Does that make sense?
Do you think there's any possibility that you might be misinterpreting the situation at the warehouse?

I mean… I guess there’s always a possibility, right? I don’t want to sound like I’m just refusing to listen. But it doesn’t feel like I’m misreading it. I came in because my husband and the people at the warehouse keep acting like I’m crazy, and… I know what I’ve seen. They watch what I’m doing, and then the pallet counts come out changed, and it keeps me from getting that supervisor spot. I’m not trying to be difficult. That’s just how it looks to me.
How long have you been feeling like they're watching you at the warehouse?

Um… it’s been a while. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but maybe around eight months? That’s when I started feeling like people were watching what I was doing and things were getting changed. Is that… is that the kind of timeframe you mean?
Would you say the idea that people at the warehouse are watching you and changing pallet counts to prevent you from getting the supervisor spot seems strange or unlikely to most people?

I mean… yeah, I can see how it probably sounds strange to other people when I say it out loud. I don’t want you to think I’m trying to be unreasonable or anything. It’s just… that’s why I came in, because my husband and people at the warehouse keep acting like I’m crazy, but I know what I’ve seen. They’ve been watching my moves, and the pallet counts keep changing, and it feels like it’s to keep me from getting that supervisor spot. Does that make sense?
Do you think the people at the warehouse would be able to change the pallet counts without other people noticing?

I mean… I know it sounds like that would be hard to do without anyone noticing. I’m not trying to say everybody there is in on it or anything. But I do think they can watch what I’m doing and change the pallet counts in ways that make it look like I messed up, or like I’m not ready for that supervisor spot. That’s why I came in, because everyone keeps acting like I’m crazy for saying it, but… I know what I’ve seen.
Do you think that things you see or hear on TV, or read in the newspaper, are specifically about you or related to you?

Not really with TV or newspapers, no… I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is. It’s more about the warehouse. That’s why I came in, because my husband and people there keep acting like I’m crazy, but I know they’ve been watching what I’m doing and changing the pallet counts to keep me from getting that supervisor spot. Is that what you mean?
Do you ever feel like things that happen to other people or events that you see are somehow related to you or meant for you?

Not like… every random thing, no. I don’t want to sound like I think the whole world is sending me messages or something. It’s mostly at work. Like when the pallet counts change after I’ve been doing everything right, or people seem to be watching what I’m doing — it feels connected to me, like it’s aimed at keeping me from that supervisor spot. That’s why I came in, because my husband and people at the warehouse keep saying I’m acting crazy, but I know what I’ve been seeing. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you think that things that happen to you at the warehouse are meant to convey a specific message to you?

I mean… not like a “message” in some weird way, I don’t think. It’s more like what happens there is showing me they’re trying to make a point, I guess. Like they’re watching what I do and then the pallet counts get changed so it looks like I’m messing up, like I’m not good enough for that supervisor spot.

That’s why I came in, because my husband and people at the warehouse keep acting like I’m crazy for saying it, but… I know what I’ve been seeing. Does that make sense?
Do you think that the actions of the people at the warehouse are specifically intended to affect you or your chances of getting the supervisor spot?

Yes… I mean, I don’t want to sound dramatic, but that is how it feels. Like they’ve been watching what I do, watching my moves, and then somehow the pallet counts get changed so it looks like I’m the one messing up.

And I know people keep saying I’m acting crazy — my husband too — but I really do think it’s meant to affect me getting that supervisor spot. That’s why I came in, because I don’t know how else to explain it.

Do you think that the people at the warehouse are changing the pallet counts because of something specific about you, rather than just trying to prevent you from getting the supervisor spot in general?

I don’t know if it’s something “about me” exactly… I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is. It’s just that I know they’ve been watching my moves, and then the pallet counts get changed, and it feels like it’s aimed at me getting that supervisor spot.

That’s why I came in, because my husband and people at the warehouse keep acting like I’m crazy for saying it, but… I know what I’ve been seeing. Is that what you’re asking?
Do you think that the people at the warehouse are watching you or changing the pallet counts because you believe you have a special role or status?

I don’t know if I’d say a “special role” or status… that sounds kind of, I don’t know, like too much. I’m not trying to say I’m important like that.

It’s more that I came in because my husband and people at the warehouse keep acting like I’m crazy, but I know they’ve been watching my moves and changing the pallet counts so I won’t get that supervisor spot. That’s what it feels like to me. Is that answering it right?
Have you ever had a time when you didn't believe people at the warehouse were watching you or changing the pallet counts?

I mean… before all this with the supervisor spot, I guess I wasn’t really thinking about it like that. But lately, no, it’s hard for me not to see it.

I know that probably sounds like I’m making it into something, and I’m not trying to be difficult, but I came in because my husband and the warehouse people keep acting like I’m crazy. I just… I know they’ve been watching my moves and changing the pallet counts to keep me from getting that spot. Is that what you mean?
Have you ever had a period of time, even if just for a day, where you didn't think people at the warehouse were watching you or changing the pallet counts?

Honestly… no, not really. I mean, I try to tell myself maybe I’m overthinking it, because I don’t want to sound unreasonable. But even if it’s just one day, it’s still kind of there in my head.

That’s why I came in, because my husband and the people at the warehouse keep acting like I’m crazy, but I know they’ve been watching what I do and messing with the pallet counts so I don’t get that supervisor spot. I’m not trying to make it sound dramatic… that’s just what I’ve been seeing.
Do you think it's possible that you could be wrong about people at the warehouse watching you and changing the pallet counts?

I mean… I guess anything’s possible, right? I don’t want to sit here and sound like I’m being stubborn or like I won’t listen.

But honestly, no… I don’t really feel like I’m wrong about it. That’s why I came in, because my husband and the people at the warehouse keep acting like I’m crazy, and I’m trying to explain it the right way. But I know they’ve been watching what I do and changing the pallet counts so I won’t get that supervisor spot. Does that make sense?
For how long have you believed that people at the warehouse are watching you and changing the pallet counts?

Um… it’s been a while. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I’d say about eight months now.

That’s when I started really feeling like people were watching me and that things, like the pallet counts, were being changed. Is that the kind of time frame you mean?
How certain are you that people at the warehouse are watching you and changing the pallet counts?

I mean… I don’t want to sound like I’m being difficult, but I’m pretty certain. Like, really certain.

That’s kind of why I came in, because my husband and people at the warehouse keep acting like I’m crazy, and I’m trying to say it in a way that makes sense… but I know they’ve been watching what I do and changing the pallet counts so I don’t get that supervisor spot. I know how that sounds, but that’s what’s been happening.

Would you describe the idea that people at the warehouse are watching you and changing pallet counts as something that sounds strange or unbelievable to you, or does it seem completely normal and realistic?

I mean… I know it probably sounds strange when I say it out loud. I don’t want you to think I’m trying to be dramatic or anything.

But to me, it feels realistic. That’s why I came in, because my husband and the warehouse people keep acting like I’m crazy, but I know they’ve been watching my moves and changing the pallet counts so I don’t get that supervisor spot. It doesn’t feel made up to me.
Have you ever had a moment, no matter how brief, where you doubted that people at the warehouse were watching you or changing the pallet counts?

Maybe for a second here and there I think, like… am I saying this the wrong way, or am I making it sound bad? But I don’t really doubt what’s happening.

I came in because my husband and the people at the warehouse keep acting like I’m crazy, and I’m trying to be reasonable about it, but I know they’ve been watching my moves and changing the pallet counts to keep me from getting that supervisor spot. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you think the belief that people at the warehouse are watching you and changing pallet counts is a strange or unusual idea to most people?

Yeah… I guess most people would probably think it sounds unusual. I get that. I’m not trying to sound paranoid or make trouble.

But from where I’m standing, it’s not some random idea. I came in because my husband and people at the warehouse keep acting like I’m crazy, and I’m just trying to explain it right… but I really do think they’ve been watching what I do and changing the pallet counts so I don’t get that supervisor spot. Does that make sense what I’m saying?

I came in because my husband and people at the warehouse keep acting like I’m crazy, and I’m just trying to explain it right… but I really do think they’ve been watching what I do and changing the pallet counts so I don’t get that supervisor spot. Does that make sense what I’m saying?

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with persistent delusional thoughts of being watched and conspired against at the warehouse, which have been ongoing for approximately eight months. These thoughts are not deemed bizarre and are within the realm of possibility, aligning more closely with delusional disorder.
